integrity: The Pearson gap is reconstructed as the determinant of the standardized moment Gram matrix and factorized through a weighted Vandermonde determinant. The fixed-mass optimizer is obtained from an explicit derivative factorization whose cubic has exactly one positive root. Exact-rational computation replays these identities and does not substitute for the proof.
scientific_limitations: The fixed-profile optimization is for exactly three distinct atoms with positive masses.
For four or more atoms the same moment Gram determinant becomes a sum of squared Vandermonde minors, so the single-ratio optimization does not carry over directly.
The 1989 Rohatgi-Szekely article was available only at abstract/bibliographic level in the checked access routes.
title: Vandermonde factorization and exact support optimum for the Pearson skewness–kurtosis gap
